questions.prompt: What question does Anthropic say a regression eval asks?

options.text: What is the best result the model can reach, given enough tries?
options.explanation: That is closer to a capability question. A regression eval asks about tasks it used to handle.

options.text: Does the agent still handle all the tasks that it used to handle?
options.explanation: Right. This is Anthropic's question for regression evals, which should have a nearly 100% pass rate.

options.text: Which of two models do users prefer when they see both results?
options.explanation: That is an A/B comparison, covered in chapter 4. It is not the regression question.

questions.prompt: What does OpenAI say continuous evaluation should do?

options.text: Run evals on every change, watch for nondeterminism, and grow the eval set over time
options.explanation: Right. These are the three parts in OpenAI's description.

options.text: Run evals only before a launch, and then stop them once the product is live
options.explanation: OpenAI says to run evals on every change, not only before a launch.

options.text: Replace human review with automatic scores, so that nobody needs to look at outputs
options.explanation: OpenAI says to use human feedback to calibrate automated scoring.

options.text: The chance that at least one of k tries gives a good result
options.explanation: That is pass@k. Anthropic describes it as a different metric.

options.text: The average score of one output across k separate reviewers
options.explanation: The metric is about repeated trials, not about reviewers.

options.text: The probability that all k of the repeated trials succeed
options.explanation: Right. It matters when users expect good results every time.
